items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lem:halt-if-valid at source lines 1861-1864: if the sentence T(M,w) implies E(M,w) is valid, then M halts on input w. The proof at source lines 1866-1894 is the semantic converse of a syntactic reduction and is not a routine computation. It has to build the specific Lang L_M-structure M with domain the natural numbers which interprets 0 as zero, the prime function as successor, < as less-than, and the predicates Q_q and S_sigma as the sets of pairs (m,n) recording where the machine is at time n; then instantiate the assumed validity at that structure and at a suitable variable assignment, translate the satisfaction of T(M,w) into the fact that the structure describes the run, unpack the satisfaction of the existential E(M,w) into a pair (q,sigma) with delta undefined, and finally read that back as a genuine halting computation. Each of those translations is a separate step and none of them is stated in the counted lemma. No result outside the retained text is used.
